metadata.title: Palbociclib Therapy - 28 day
metadata.indication: Palbociclib in combination with an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant for eligible HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Only entered values are assessed; omitted clinical domains remain explicitly unassessed.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciled · independent clinical and pharmacy validation pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: NCCP00414 v5a pp1–5 and EMA Ibrance SmPC reconciled; AI-assisted source checks are not clinical authorisation.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.
metadata.schedule_summary: The usual palbociclib starting dose is 125 mg once daily; a lower dose may be prescribed. Palbociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, then paused on Days 22–28 of each 28-day cycle. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily, or fulvestrant follows its injection schedule. Ovarian suppression has its own plan when required.
metadata.source_schedule_interval_label: 28 days; oral targeted treatment on Days 1–21

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding of the current NCCP source. It does not replace the NCCP regimen, clinical judgement, local policy, prescribing review or pharmacy verification.

anc.label: ANC (×10⁹/L)
anc.source_grading_note: NCCP 00414 v5a Tables 2 and 4 cite CTCAE v4.0. Source-specific descriptions and thresholds are retained; no CTCAE v5/v6 automatic grading, substituted descriptors or linked comparison panels are applied.
anc.assessment_guidance: NCCP Table 2: ANC 0.5 to <1.0 ×10⁹/L is grade 3; ANC <0.5 is grade 4. ANC ≥1.0 meets this isolated count criterion only. Grade 3 action depends on Day 1 versus Day 15 of cycles 1–2, fever/infection and recovery. Missing platelets and other domains remain unassessed.

platelets.label: Platelets (×10⁹/L)
platelets.source_grading_note: NCCP 00414 v5a Tables 2 and 4 cite CTCAE v4.0. Source-specific descriptions and thresholds are retained; no CTCAE v5/v6 automatic grading, substituted descriptors or linked comparison panels are applied.
platelets.assessment_guidance: NCCP Table 2: platelets 25 to <50 ×10⁹/L is grade 3; <25 is grade 4. Platelets ≥50 meets this isolated count criterion only. Grade 3 action depends on cycle timing; missing ANC and other domains remain unassessed.

assessment_day.label: Assessment timing
assessment_day.help_text: Day 15 continuation applies only to cycles 1–2. Enter counts independently if timing is unknown; the result will explain the timing needed.

fever_or_infection.label: Fever ≥38.5°C and/or infection with grade 3 neutropenia
fever_or_infection.help_text: Select Yes for documented grade 3 neutropenia (ANC 0.5 to <1.0 ×10⁹/L) with fever ≥38.5°C and/or infection. This is the protocol dose-modification definition, not a threshold for delaying urgent infection assessment; follow the local fever emergency pathway.
fever_or_infection.source_grading_note: NCCP 00414 v5a Tables 2 and 4 cite CTCAE v4.0. Source-specific descriptions and thresholds are retained; no CTCAE v5/v6 automatic grading, substituted descriptors or linked comparison panels are applied. The NCCP 38.5°C dose-table condition differs from the NCI CTCAE v4.03 febrile-neutropenia definition; do not relabel the NCCP condition as that CTCAE term.
fever_or_infection.assessment_guidance: This is the NCCP Table 2 treatment-modification event: grade 3 neutropenia (ANC 0.5 to <1.0 ×10⁹/L) with fever ≥38.5°C and/or infection. It is not an automatic NCI febrile-neutropenia grade or an emergency-contact threshold; suspected sepsis requires immediate assessment under local policy.

prolonged_or_recurrent_grade3.label: Prolonged (>1 week) or recurrent grade 3 neutropenia on Day 1
prolonged_or_recurrent_grade3.source_grading_note: NCCP 00414 v5a Tables 2 and 4 cite CTCAE v4.0. Source-specific descriptions and thresholds are retained; no CTCAE v5/v6 automatic grading, substituted descriptors or linked comparison panels are applied.
prolonged_or_recurrent_grade3.assessment_guidance: In NCCP Table 2, grade 3 neutropenia is ANC 0.5 to <1.0 ×10⁹/L. Recovery taking >1 week, or recurrent grade 3 neutropenia on Day 1 of subsequent cycles, prompts consideration of dose reduction; this is clinical event history, not a numeric grade calculator.

nonhaem_toxicity_grade.label: Non-haematological toxicity grade (NCCP CTCAE v4.0)

options.label: Grade 0 — no toxicity
options.description: No non-haematological adverse event reported; this is a no-event option, not a formal CTCAE severity grade.

options.label: Grade 1 — mild
options.description: Generally mild or asymptomatic, with observation alone. Confirm grade 1 against the named CTCAE v4.0-series event; this general anchor is not an event-specific definition.

options.label: Grade 2 — moderate
options.description: Generally moderate, requiring limited or non-invasive treatment or affecting instrumental daily activities. Confirm the named event’s CTCAE v4.0-series grade 2 criterion.

options.label: Grade 3 — severe
options.description: Generally severe or medically significant, potentially requiring admission or limiting self-care. Confirm the actual event’s CTCAE v4.0-series grade 3 criterion; a general severity label is insufficient.

options.label: Grade 4 — life-threatening
options.description: Generally life-threatening and requiring urgent intervention. Confirm the named event’s CTCAE v4.0-series grade 4 criterion; some event terms do not have every grade.

nonhaem_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Document the named adverse event and use its own CTCAE v4.0-series criterion (NCI v4.03 reference). The general severity anchors below are screening aids only; not all grades apply to every event. New pulmonary symptoms / severe ILD use their separate palbociclib rules. This field does not calculate a grade from blood tests.
nonhaem_toxicity_grade.source_grading_note: NCCP 00414 v5a Tables 2 and 4 cite CTCAE v4.0. Source-specific descriptions and thresholds are retained; no CTCAE v5/v6 automatic grading, substituted descriptors or linked comparison panels are applied. NCI v4.03 is the published v4.0-series reference (14 June 2010). Its introductory severity anchors do not replace each named adverse-event definition.

nonhaem_persists_despite_treatment.label: Grade ≥3 toxicity persists despite medical treatment
nonhaem_persists_despite_treatment.source_grading_note: NCCP 00414 v5a Tables 2 and 4 cite CTCAE v4.0. Source-specific descriptions and thresholds are retained; no CTCAE v5/v6 automatic grading, substituted descriptors or linked comparison panels are applied.
nonhaem_persists_despite_treatment.assessment_guidance: Confirm that the already named and graded CTCAE v4.0-series non-haematological event remains grade ≥3 despite medical treatment. This yes/no field records response to treatment; it does not assign a new grade.

renal_band.label: Renal function category

options.label: CrCl ≥15 mL/min — no protocol dose adjustment required
CrCl <15 mL/min / end-stage renal disease — limited evidence; specialist review

renal_band.assessment_guidance: NCCP Table 3 expects no dose adjustment for renal impairment or haemodialysis. EMA has insufficient haemodialysis data; severe end-stage disease needs individual oncology/pharmacy review. No automatic renal dose reduction is encoded.

new_or_worsening_pulmonary_symptoms.label: New or worsening cough, breathlessness or hypoxia suggesting ILD / pneumonitis

strong_cyp3a_inhibitor.label: Strong CYP3A inhibitor in current medicines
strong_cyp3a_inhibitor.help_text: Avoid where possible; if unavoidable the oncologist/pharmacist confirms 75 mg daily and return to previous dose after inhibitor washout. Do not extrapolate to an already reduced dose without review.

strong_cyp3a_inducer.label: Strong CYP3A inducer in current medicines

critical_visceral_disease.label: Critical visceral disease / visceral crisis
critical_visceral_disease.help_text: Efficacy and safety were not studied in this setting; requires specialist treatment-selection review.

further_reduction_required.label: Further dose reduction has been clinically determined to be required
further_reduction_required.help_text: Use after reviewing the actual toxicity and recovery. Recurrent grade 3 neutropenia alone means consider reduction, not automatic discontinuation.

ovarian_suppression.label: Ovarian suppression / ablation confirmed where relevant

output_templates.proceed: No encoded contraindication or hold criterion was triggered. Complete normal prescribing and pharmacy checks.

supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
premedication_summary: Routine premedication is not usually required.
other_supportive_care: No routine premedication; oral minimal–low emetic risk, with rescue support according to local policy.
Provide fever/infection and new pulmonary-symptom advice; do not use the 38.5°C dose-table value as a delay threshold for seeking help.
Check CYP3A interactions, avoid grapefruit and St John’s Wort.
Endocrine partner and ovarian suppression have separate prescriptions and monitoring requirements.
supportive_care.mapping_basis: NCCP 00414 current supportive-care section, source checked 2026-10-25; local oral-SACT policy and individual interactions apply.

ctcae_standard.reference: NCCP 00414 v5a cites CTCAE v4.0 in Tables 2 and 4; NCI CTCAE v4.03 is the supporting v4-series reference.
ctcae_standard.display_requirement: Numeric/binary fields show the source table guidance without automated v5/v6 grading. The non-haematological selector has explicit general v4-series anchors and requires confirmation against the named adverse-event term.

administration.notes: No palbociclib on Days 22–28. Capsule: take with food; tablets may be taken with or without food per EMA. Check formulation. Endocrine partner continues on its own schedule. Do not replace a missed/vomited dose.

indications.description: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer with an aromatase inhibitor.
HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer with fulvestrant in women with prior endocrine therapy.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile before starting (NCCP p2).
Confirm HR/HER2, endocrine partner, menopausal state, suppression plan, pregnancy/breastfeeding exclusion and interacting medicines.
early_cycles: FBC on Day 1 and Day 15 of cycles 1–2 (NCCP p2).
If grade 3 cytopenia is present on Day 15 of cycles 1–2, repeat FBC on Day 22; if grade 3 on Day 1, withhold and repeat within 1 week.
regular: FBC Day 1 from cycle 3; renal/liver profile before each cycle (NCCP p2).
Only if no worse than grade 1/2 neutropenia during the first 6 cycles, subsequent FBC may be every 3 months, before the beginning of a cycle, and whenever clinically indicated (NCCP p2).
Ask about fever/infection, cough/breathlessness, tolerability and medicines at reviews.
monitoring.disease: Response imaging follows the consultant treatment plan; NCCP does not mandate a fixed CT or tumour-marker interval.
monitoring.heart: No routine palbociclib-only ECG or echo timetable is specified. Investigate symptoms/risk or requirements of other medicines when indicated.
monitoring.bone: Bone-density/fracture assessment depends on the endocrine partner, ovarian suppression and individual fracture risk. Add the partner-specific plan, not a universal palbociclib DXA interval.

source_discrepancies.detail: NCCP expects no dose adjustment including haemodialysis; EMA states insufficient haemodialysis evidence. Review individually, with no fabricated reduction.
NCCP v5a describes capsules with food. EMA includes tablets, which may be taken with or without food. Confirm the dispensed formulation.
